title: Singular Proxies for Adaptive Caching in Diffusion Language Models
claim: A cheap low-dimensional proxy reveals the same hidden-state drift as the costly full output, while the raw inputs look uniformly stable.
layout: 3 heatmap panels side-by-side, shared colorbar, left-to-right comparison of states
description: Three square heatmaps sit side by side under the shared title 'Adjacent-Step Similarity of LLaDA-8B-Instruct (layer 12)'. Each plots decoding step (y-axis) against token index (x-axis), colored by cosine similarity from 0 to 1, using a green-to-dark-blue scale shown in a colorbar on the right. The left panel, input states (d=4096), is almost uniformly pale green, meaning high similarity, with only a faint diagonal. The middle panel, the singular proxy (r=128), shows a bright diagonal band and horizontal streaks of dark blue where similarity drops. The right panel, FFN output states (d=4096), shows nearly the same pattern as the middle one. The eye goes first to the dark streaks in the middle and right panels, which contrast with the washed-out left panel.
caption: Adjacent-Step Similarities for LLaDA-8B-Instruct [ref]. While input states exhibit uniformly high similarity, our singular proxy at early stage of the layer can efficiently uncover the drifts in the final FFN output. This provides a clear guidance for selective hidden state updates.
abstract: While Diffusion Language Models (DLMs) offer a flexible, arbitrary-order alternative to the autoregressive paradigm, their non-causal nature precludes standard KV caching, forcing costly hidden state recomputation at every decoding step. Existing DLM caching approaches reduce this cost by selective hidden state updates; however, they are still limited by (i) costly token-wise update identification heuristics and (ii) rigid, uniform budget allocation that fails to account for heterogeneous hidden state dynamics. To address these challenges, we present SPA-Cache that jointly optimizes update identification and budget allocation in DLM cache. First, we derive a low-dimensional singular proxy that enables the identification of update-critical tokens in a low-dimensional subspace, substantially reducing the overhead of update identification. Second, we introduce an adaptive strategy that allocates fewer updates to stable layers without degrading generation quality. Together, these contributions significantly improve the efficiency of DLMs, yielding up to an $8\times$ throughput improvement over vanilla decoding and a $2$--$4\times$ speedup over existing caching baselines.
